fields.name: caveat
values: Like-for-like is held on FOUR axes: 55-inch class · 3840x2160 (true 4K/UHD, not 1080p) · LED-backlit LCD (no OLED on either side) · mass-market brand's ENTRY 4K smart-TV line. 2016 anchor = VIZIO E55u-D0, the 55-inch Ultra HD model of VIZIO's cheapest 2016 SmartCast line, MSRP $699.99. 2026 anchor = TCL 55Q651G, the 55-inch model of TCL's cheapest current 4K line, $319.96-$319.99 street. THREE ASTERISKS, stated rather than hidden: (1) The 2016 figure is a manufacturer MSRP at announcement; the 2026 figure is a shelf price. Street prices fell inside 2016 too — TechRadar's review of the LG 55UH7700 quotes $999 against a $1,799 launch MSRP — so the true street-to-street fall is smaller than MSRP-to-street. (2) The 2026 set is BETTER, not merely cheaper (QLED, HDR10+/HLG, Google TV, higher brightness), so this understates the per-unit-quality collapse; the BLS constant-quality televisions index fell 67.1% over the same window. (3) TIER TRAP AVOIDED: the well-known Vizio E55-D0 is 1080p, NOT 4K — the 4K sibling is the E55u-D0 and it cost $130 more ($699.99 vs $569.99). Both figures appear in the same press release and in the artifact screenshot. A tier-matched premium check is carried as claims c3/c4 so the entry-tier headline cannot be read as cherry-picking.
